content.title: Headings Create a Reading Path
content.hook: A page is easier to use when its structure is obvious. Headings are not decorative labels. They create a hierarchy for the content.
content.context: Use one main page heading for the page’s primary subject, then use lower-level headings for sections and subsections.
goals: Create a logical heading structure and understand that source order and heading meaning help people navigate content.

content.question: Which heading order best represents one page with two major sections?

feedback.correct: The first heading establishes the main subject. The two major sections are children of that subject, so h2 is the natural level for both.
feedback.incorrect: The first heading establishes the main subject. The two major sections are children of that subject, so h2 is the natural level for both.

activities.title: Do not choose headings by size

content.title: Do not choose headings by size
content.text:
If a design wants a small-looking section title, do not pick h4 just because h4 is visually smaller. Heading level is about structure. Visual size belongs to the presentation layer you already learned.

This separation keeps your document meaningful even when the visual design changes.

options.text: h1 → h2 → h3 is always required even when there are no subsections.
Heading levels should reflect the content hierarchy; do not skip around just to get a certain visual size.
All headings should be h6 for consistency.
Headings should only be used on pages with images.

feedback.correct: Use levels to communicate the structure of the content, not the size of the text.
feedback.incorrect: Use levels to communicate the structure of the content, not the size of the text.
